title: The One Feature Cairo's Developers Liked in a Product They Hated
conflicts: Founding year: 2012 (TechCrunch Feb 2016, CairoScene, Wamda's Sept 2012 AStarApps date) vs 2014 (LBS, MENAbytes); story uses 2012 and dates the pivot by Wamda's April 2013 report. Flat6Labs money: $10,000 (The National) vs $11,000 (AUC Business Forward); story uses $10,000. Scale numbers differ by date (12,000 apps/100m devices Feb 2016; ~300m devices June 2016; 25,000 apps/2.5bn devices 2020) and are not used. Profitability reported as 'profitable', 'almost profitable' and 'touching profitability' in 2020 sources; left out. Gabr's '100 applications on the first day' after the Hacker News video is his later recollection; the April 2013 Show HN threads I found drew modest replies, so the figure is attributed to him.
notes: Episode re-centred from 'joining Y Combinator' (2016) to the documented 2012-13 forced pivot from AStarApps to the shake-to-report tool; YC W16 and the Accel seed round are covered as the outcome. Arc changed from founding-decision to change-of-direction. Fast Company and VentureBeat coverage of the 2013 visa episode block automated requests, so it rests on CairoScene.
